archetypes.name: harness-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan hinges on an existing shell harness, gh shim, renderer stub, and fallback function contracts that could drift from the proposed test steps.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the proposed test fixture, renderer-stub save/restore flow, gh shim expectations, and fallback assertions against the actual write-final-report harness contracts. Look for wrong variable names, fixture paths, helper assumptions, ordering hazards, or assertions that would not exercise the intended LINES_DATA_OK=true fallback branch. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: retro-scope
archetypes.rationale: The issue asks for retroactive plan and acceptance criteria, while the scoped repo edits are only harness files, so scope-evidence alignment needs targeted review.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check whether the written plan adequately satisfies the requested retroactive plan/acceptance-criteria deliverable without implying unscoped production or documentation edits. Verify that any decision to keep documentation in the plan body rather than repo files is consistent with the issue description, scope file list, and repository conventions. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: metrics-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan documents API pagination, input validation, timeout posture, and degradation behavior for a live PR-metrics feature that may have contract drift.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the plan's stated PR-metrics contracts against the repository evidence for compute-pr-line-counts, render-run-summary, and write-final-report integration. Focus on mismatches in REPO/PR_NUMBER validation, gh api --paginate behavior, timeout/degradation claims, bucket semantics, and whether acceptance criteria are test-pinned as claimed. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
